purpose: Flecainide is used to treat certain types of irregular heartbeats, also called arrhythmias. It helps keep your heart beating in a normal, steady rhythm. Your doctor may prescribe it if you have conditions like atrial fibrillation, atrial flutter, or certain other fast or abnormal heart rhythms.
how_it_works: Your heart beats because of electrical signals that travel through it in an organized way. Sometimes those signals go haywire and cause your heart to beat too fast or irregularly. Flecainide works by slowing down those electrical signals and making it harder for the abnormal ones to fire, which helps restore a normal, steady heartbeat.
common_side_effects: Some people notice dizziness, lightheadedness, or blurred vision, especially when starting the medication. You might also experience headache, nausea, or feeling short of breath. Some people notice a slight tremor or feel unusually tired. These effects are often mild and may improve over time.
warnings: This medication can sometimes cause new or worsened heart rhythm problems, especially in people who have had a heart attack or have structural heart disease, so it is very important your doctor knows your full heart history. Never stop taking flecainide suddenly without talking to your doctor first. Tell your doctor right away if you feel your heart racing, pounding, fluttering, or if you feel faint or have chest pain. Also let your doctor know about all other medications you take, as many drugs can interact with flecainide.
typical_dosing: Flecainide is usually taken by mouth twice a day, roughly every 12 hours, with or without food. A common starting dose is 50 mg twice daily, and your doctor may slowly increase it based on how you respond, up to a maximum of 300 mg per day. Always take it exactly as prescribed and try to take it at the same times each day.
